regime.call: Rate-shock risk-off spreads while chip resilience holds

risk_appetite.evidence: SPX fell 0.76% to 7,706.03 and IWM/SPY dropped 1.13% to 0.3672, while SOX rose 0.81% to 12,534.27 and TAIEX gained 1.14% to 47,718.84 — a bifurcated tape, not clean risk-on or risk-off.

liquidity.evidence: US 10Y yield rose 15bps to 5.11% (highest since 2007) and DXY climbed 0.66% to 101.09, an 8-week high, while NFCI ticked up to -0.555 from -0.557.

volatility.evidence: VIX rose 2.08% to 15.18 and VVIX rose 3.30% to 88.60, while SKEW climbed 2.78% to 146.15, near its 5-day high of 148.1.

confirms: US 10Y yield hit 5.11% (+15bps), the highest since 2007, driving the S&P 500 down 0.76% to 7,706.03
Gold fell 1.23% to $4,322.70 and Bitcoin fell 2.03% to $84,422.80 simultaneously, consistent with a dollar-driven liquidity squeeze rather than a safe-haven rotation
DXY rose 0.66% to 101.09 on hawkish Fed repricing after Governor Barr's comments, pressuring both metals and crypto together
contradicts: SOX rose 0.81% to 12,534.27 and TAIEX rose 1.14% to 47,718.84, showing the chip complex still resilient against the rate shock
VIX remains low at 15.18 and NDX is nearly flat at -0.04%, so equity vol has not yet repriced for stress

falsifiers.meaning: Would confirm the bond-driven risk-off is deepening and threatens broader equity valuations, including chips
Would mean the chip-led resilience is breaking down alongside the rate shock
